chunks: Boost inductor flyback voltage. The question: What happens to the inductor flyback voltage? Why is this important?
When the boost switch opens, the inductor current cannot stop instantly, so the inductor's voltage reverses and the switch node shoots up.
The diode catches this: once the node reaches the output voltage plus a diode drop, the diode conducts and delivers the energy to the output.
So the flyback voltage is clamped, and it is also how a boost delivers power. If the current has nowhere to go, the voltage can reach hundreds of volts.
Imagine a cyclist coasting at speed who must suddenly stop. The rider's momentum keeps going, so the rider is thrown forward.
The inductor current is the rider, and the sudden stop is the switch opening. The diode is a soft landing mat that safely catches the rider.
Without the mat, the rider hits whatever is in the way, and a boost with no path suffers a huge voltage spike.
Before turn-off the current ran down through the switch.
After turn-off the same current continues through the inductor and takes the only remaining route, through the diode into the output.
The switch node settles at the output voltage plus one diode drop, and the inductor voltage is negative.
Flyback voltage: the voltage an inductor creates when its current is suddenly interrupted.
Switch node: the junction of the inductor, switch, and diode ("What a boost converter is"). Clamp: a path that limits the voltage, here the diode and the output.
Parasitic capacitance: tiny unwanted capacitance in the switch and wiring. Over-voltage protection (OVP): a protection that stops switching if the output gets too high.
With 5 volts in and 10 volts out, the diode clamps the switch node at about 10 plus 0. 4 equals 10. 4 volts. The inductor then sees 5-10. 4 equals -5.

"When the boost switch opens, the inductor current has to continue, so its voltage reverses and the switch node rises until the diode conducts.
That clamps the node at V out plus V F , so the flyback energy goes into the output instead of a spike.
That is both how the boost steps up and what sets the switch voltage stress.
